A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRQ-learner research. Their text, figures, table, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material and renumbered results.

before.justification: v1 reports original Taxi experiments comparing Q-function estimation errors across sample sizes, horizons and policy overlap, using unrestricted and linear model classes (Figures 4–5).

after.justification: v2 retains the original Taxi experiments and adds original Frozen Lake evaluation results in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The nuisance functions, two-stage procedure, orthogonal loss, pseudo-outcomes and Algorithm 1 are retained. Added explanations of nuisance estimation and pseudo-outcomes do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Frozen Lake trajectories and unrestricted-model Q-function evaluation alongside the retained Taxi experiments. This is a limited extension of environment coverage within the same off-policy MDP estimation task.

E2.justification: Q-regression, FQE and Minimax Q-learning remain the evaluated comparators in the Taxi experiments. Figure 6 extends this same comparator set to Frozen Lake.

E3.justification: The new Frozen Lake sample-size sweep uses n = 50, 100, 200 and 500, while Taxi retains 2000–6000. v2 also explicitly quantifies policy overlap using the summed minimum of policy probabilities. The rMSE metric and documented Taxi settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 extends the existing sensitivity tests for sample size, horizon and policy overlap to Frozen Lake. The Taxi analyses, including unrestricted versus linear model classes, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means with one standard error over five runs with different seeds. v2 retains this reporting practice without changing run counts or introducing additional uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds Frozen Lake rMSE results across three sweeps, showing DRQ below the plug-in baselines across the sample-size and horizon sweeps. The six matched Taxi panels in Figures 4–5 retain their result curves.

T1.justification: The identification results, orthogonality theorem, quasi-oracle bound, double-robustness corollary and appendix proofs are retained in substance. Identification theorems become lemmas, assumptions move to Appendix B, and Appendix D.1.1 explains existing pseudo-outcomes without adding a derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a flexible DRQ-learner with double robustness, Neyman orthogonality and quasi-oracle efficiency, applicable to discrete and continuous states. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains Q-regression's advantage at large epsilon in Figure 5 through shrinking density ratios and explicitly qualifies DRQ's finite-sample dominance. It also adds discussion of nuisance-estimation difficulty, history-augmented states and pseudo-outcome mechanisms, and clarifies that fairness constraints are not imposed by design.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes figure/table reproduction scripts and adds a future public-code-release statement. The repository address, oracle density-ratio disclosure and Taxi hyperparameter table remain unchanged. Frozen Lake-specific implementation settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds Hess et al. (2026), Overlap-weighted orthogonal meta-learner for treatment effect estimation over time. New discussion connects the MDP formulation to contextual bandits and dynamic treatment regimes; the principal novelty comparisons remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, moves identification assumptions into a new Additional Details appendix, adds pseudo-outcome intuition, and introduces ethics and reproducibility statements. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from the wide preprint template to the narrower ICLR layout, resizing and relocating retained displays. Figure 6 adds three panels, while Figures 4–5 gain secondary overlap axes and environment-specific captions.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens empirical support through Frozen Lake and improves explanations and performance qualifications, particularly Figure 5's high-epsilon exception. These gains are limited by incomplete documentation of the added experiment: Section 6 retains Taxi's sample-size range, and Appendix E/Table 1 still describe only Taxi.
